A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CryoFastAR study. The methods, experiments, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E can be reliably matched despite layout changes and relocation of the references.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulated and experimental cryo-EM reconstruction results, including pose errors, resolutions, runtimes, and analyses of input-view counts and noise levels.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental measurements in Tables 1–2 and the reconstruction, FSC, and sensitivity results in Figures 3–6, including Appendix A.

M1.justification: The reported inference procedure in Section 4.3 changes from using the first view as reference to selecting among 64 candidates by their average confidence against fixed target views. The encoder, decoder, Fourier planar-map representation, training loss, and pose-regression procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both retain training on 113,600 PDB structures and the same simulated Spliceosome, Spike, and FA and experimental RAG, 50S, and Spliceosome evaluations. Naming CryoCRAB as the CTF source does not establish different represented data or task coverage; the specified parameter count and simulation conditions remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains CryoSPIN, CryoDRGN2, CryoSPARC, and refined CryoSPARC; Table 2 retains the same comparisons without CryoSPIN. Adding SGD to the description of CryoSPARC does not change its evaluated implementation or settings, which remain identical in Appendix C.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 changes the stated progressive training-view range from 2–16 to 2–32, resolving an inconsistency with v1's Section 4.3, which already mentions training with 32 views. This is a reported setting revision; the PDFs do not establish that training was rerun. Splits, metrics, epoch budgets, and 128-view inference batches remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.2 and Figure 5 retain the same sensitivity analyses using 16, 32, 64, and 128 views and SNR levels 0.05, 0.1, and 1.0. No new ablation or robustness experiment evaluates the reference-selection step.

E5.justification: Appendix C in both versions reports running CryoSPIN three times and selecting the best result. Neither version adds seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: Every numerical entry in Tables 1–2 matches, including the unrefined FA result of 6.64 angstroms in 01:21. The reconstruction images and plotted results in Figures 3–6 are also unchanged. No new performance measurements accompany the inference revision.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(18) retain their mathematical content. The expanded explanation of Fourier planar maps clarifies the existing representation without redefining it. Appendix B.3 reformats the CTF equation to eliminate clipping; the underlying formula is unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claims remain the first geometric foundation model for direct cryo-EM pose prediction, Fourier planar-map prediction with progressive training, and competitive reconstruction quality with substantially faster inference. Although omitted from the conclusion, the claim that pose estimation requires no precomputed CTF parameters remains elsewhere.

C2.justification: Section 6 removes the explicit limitation that CryoFastAR does not support heterogeneous reconstruction. Section 4.3 newly explains the importance of avoiding poor or junk reference particles and replaces the claim of arbitrary-view-count generalization with the narrower observation that more views improve performance. The domain-gap and batch-size limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the 64-candidate reference-selection rule and names CryoCRAB as the CTF source in Section 5, while Appendix E still cites DRACO. It removes the promises to release code, models, and datasets without supplying replacement access instructions. This does not establish that previously accessible resources were withdrawn.

R1.justification: v2 adds the CryoCRAB dataset paper as reference [5] and removes the CUT3R paper, Continuous 3D Perception Model with Persistent State, previously cited in the limitations. The main positioning relative to iterative cryo-EM reconstruction and geometric foundation models remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 locally expands the planar-map explanation, revises inference and discussion prose, adds author email addresses and acknowledgments, and moves references after the appendices. Most paragraphs and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are restyled, Figure 5 moves from the left to the right column, and text reflows around retained displays. Equation (14) now wraps within the page instead of extending beyond its edge. The benchmark table structures and result-figure content remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The explicit reference-selection procedure, reconciliation of the training-view count, clearer planar-map explanation, and repaired CTF-equation layout modestly improve reproducibility, consistency, and readability. The empirical evidence is unchanged, so no performance improvement is established. Removing the explicit heterogeneous-reconstruction limitation and resource-release commitments reduces transparency and limits the overall gain.
